subject: Recap & next steps: inference sizing, regional pricing, and residency impact
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kate Barnes <kbarnes@fintrust.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@fintrust.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-28T15:03:00-04:00
Subject: Recap & next steps: inference sizing, regional pricing, and residency impact

Hi Kate / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the concrete next steps we discussed so we have alignment before I share a more formal proposal. High-level notes first, then unit-econ calc and asks.

Call notes (TL;DR):
- Workload: customer-facing summarization + search re-ranking; generation dominant.
- Per-request profile: avg prompt ~350 tokens, avg model output ~750 tokens (generation-heavy).
- Estimated monthly volume (your initial): ~150M generation tokens + ~30M embedding tokens for search signals.
- Primary region: US (would like EU option later for EEA users/data residency).

Key commercial questions we flagged on the call:
1) Target budget range for inference (monthly committed spend)? You mentioned a ballpark but can you confirm a firm range.
2) Target unit cost expectation (rough $/1M tokens) so we can size reserved vs hosted.
3) If EU residency required, what fraction of traffic must remain in EU (all EU users? subset?) — this materially affects cost.

Initial unit-econ (very rough) — assumptions: 150M gen tokens + 30M embedding tokens / month; conservative per-request token mix as above.
- Total tokens/month (generation + embeddings): ~180M tokens.
- At target unit price of $120 per 1M tokens (US): monthly = 180 * $120 = $21,600.
- EU region premium: historically ~1.15x–1.25x on similar infra due to region pricing/higher infra costs and cross-region traffic. At 1.2x -> effective $144/1M => $25,920/month.
- Private deployment / on-prem or VPC with strict residency + KMS: typical premium +20%–30% on top of region rate (operational & compliance overhead).

Ways to bridge gaps from budget -> workable options (we discussed during call):
- Reserved capacity commit (Dedicated) reduces unit cost by ~20% at a 6–12 month commit.
- Quantization and smaller model variants for lower-latency paths: can reduce token unit cost ~15%–35% depending on quality requirements.
- Caching / prefix KV reuse on chat-like flows reduces billed tokens for repeated context by up to 30% in some workloads.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm monthly committed budget range and whether 180M tokens/month is the right baseline.
2) Confirm EU residency scope (percent of traffic / user segments).
3) I'll send a short pricing snapshot (US vs EU vs Private) + an example Dedicated commit that hits the lower unit economics, and a sample MAAP (minimal action plan) for a 30-day eval environment.

Attachments: I attached a simple estimates workbook (FinTrust_estimates.xlsx) and a Redwood pricing snapshot (redwood-pricing-us-eu-snapshot.csv).

If this looks good I'll follow up with two concrete pricing scenarios: Hosted (pay-as-you-go), Dedicated reserve (6 or 12 month), and Private (VPC) with residency premium and implementation notes.

Best,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Kate Barnes <kbarnes@fintrust.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@fintrust.com>
Date: 2026-05-29T09:18:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: inference sizing, regional pricing, and residency impact

Sean — thanks for the clear recap. Couple clarifications and confirmers from our side:

1) Volume: the 150M generation token estimate is our current best guess for Q3 steady state. It could be up to +20% if adoption spikes — please size for 180M as a conservative option. Embeddings we expect ~30M/month as noted.

2) Budget: our initial procurement band for proof-of-concept + small production is $12k–18k / month. If committed savings bring us below $10k/month at peak volumes we'd consider a larger buy-in.

3) Residency: EU residency will be required for EU customers only — roughly 25% of traffic in your baseline. We will not require full-on air-gap or on-prem for now, but must ensure EU data processing stays in-region and logs are retained per EU policy.

4) Compliance: we will share a short security/compliance questionnaire separately; Tom will own that. Note: we will likely ask for SOC2 Type II and an outline of your data retention and KMS practices during procurement.

Action items for you: please send the two priced scenarios you mentioned (hosted vs dedicated commit) with a quick calc showing monthly cost at both US and EU rates and the incremental cost to have 25% traffic in EU. Also include estimation of how much caching/prefix reuse we should expect to see vs the raw token estimate (we typically get 15%–25% reuse in our flows).

Thanks,
Kate
Kate Barnes
Head of Product, FinTrust
kbarnes@fintrust.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kate Barnes <kbarnes@fintrust.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@fintrust.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-30T09:36:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: inference sizing, regional pricing, and residency impact

Kate / Tom — perfect, thanks for the clarifications. Below is the compact priced view you asked for plus assumptions and recommended next steps. I’ll follow with a pdf that lays out the Dedicated commit tiers.

Assumptions (used in the table below):
- Baseline tokens: 180M / month (150M generation + 30M embeddings).
- EU traffic: 25% of total tokens routed to EU.
- Cache/prefix reuse reduction: mid-case 20% (so billable tokens = 0.8 * raw tokens).

Scenario A — Hosted (no commitment):
- US list price (baseline): $120 / 1M billable tokens.
- EU premium: 1.2x -> $144 / 1M.
- Effective billed tokens after 20% reuse: 180M * 0.8 = 144M billable tokens.
- Split: 75% US (108M) at $120/1M = $12,960; 25% EU (36M) at $144/1M = $5,184.
- Total monthly = $18,144.

Scenario B — Dedicated (6–12 mo commit, example 12mo tier):
- Committed price reduction: ~20% off list.
- US committed price: $96 / 1M; EU committed price (1.2x) = $115.20 / 1M.
- Same reuse and split: billable tokens 144M => US 108M at $96 = $10,368; EU 36M at $115.20 = $4,147.20.
- Total monthly = $14,515.20.

Private/VPC with residency (if you require additional isolation & customer-managed KMS):
- Apply an implementation & infra premium typically +25% on top of the committed or hosted unit price due to additional ops, certs, and audit support.
- Example (using the committed band above): US $96 *1.25 = $120 / 1M; EU $115.20 *1.25 = $144 / 1M (these map back to the hosted-like EU price).

Implications vs your stated budget ($12k–18k/month):
- Hosted mid-case ($18.1k) sits at top of your band — close but slightly over.
- Dedicated 12mo example ($14.5k) lands squarely in the range; with a 6mo or larger commit we can push unit economics further down.
- If we can increase expected cache/reuse from 20% -> 30% you save another ~18% on monthly spend.

Recommendations / next steps:
1) If you’re comfortable with a 12mo commit we can get you into the $14k–15k band; I’ll draft a sample commitment schedule showing ramp and credits.
2) If you prefer staging in Hosted first, we can run a 30-day eval in US, enable EU routing for 25% traffic, and produce actual billable token numbers before you sign a commit.
3) As you flagged — share your security questionnaire; we’ll slot a short SOC2 overview and KMS notes.

I attached the snapshot CSV (redwood-pricing-us-eu-snapshot.csv) and a quick estimates workbook. If helpful I can also run a delta calc that shows combined committed price + 30% cache/reuse outcomes so you can pick the model that best fits procurement thresholds.

Available for a follow-up tomorrow afternoon to walk through the commit scenarios live.

Best,
Sean

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-30T10:12:00-04:00
Subject: Fwd: Recap & next steps: inference sizing, regional pricing, and residency impact

Marissa — forwarding the thread after sending the committed vs hosted snapshot. Key points: FinTrust baseline 180M tokens/month, EU ~25% traffic, budget band $12k–18k. Dedicated 12mo commit example gets them to ~$14.5k/mo (good fit), hosted ends up ~$18.1k/mo. They will send security questionnaire (Tom).

Ask: can you review the 12mo commitment template and pricing tiers I plan to send (I’ll share the draft via the internal pricing drive) and flag anything I should avoid promising? Also want to confirm the discounting guardrails for a cross-region (US+EU) split and private/VPC premium.

Thanks — I’ll hold the follow-up until I get your signoff.

Sean
